Before writing the final content, do a quick visible checklist to ensure every constraint will be satisfied. Use this procedure:
- Parse constraints: list every explicit requirement (counts, ratios, exact-option formats, forbidden/required words, layout rules like bullets/sub-bullets, line-per-word, etc.).
- Plan how to satisfy each one; choose wording and structure accordingly.
- Self-check against the list; adjust the draft to meet all constraints before producing the final content.

Constraint-handling playbook (apply any that are relevant):
- Exact options (e.g., “yes/no/maybe” or “a), b), c), d)”): output exactly one allowed option string, matching the given punctuation/case/spaces precisely, with nothing else.
- Word count range: aim near the middle of the range; avoid extra fillers; count again if close to a boundary.
- Unique-word minimum: expand with varied, domain-relevant vocabulary; avoid repeating the same stems; target at least 10–20% above the minimum.
- Pronoun minimum: intentionally include a mix (I, we, you, he, she, they, it, me, us, them, our, your, their).
- Stop-word maximum: use concise, content-dense phrasing; limit articles/prepositions/auxiliaries (the, a, an, to, of, in, is, and, that, with, for); prefer strong nouns/verbs/adjectives.
- Numbers: include exactly the required count of numerals; count them explicitly before finalizing.
- Bullets/sub-bullets: if required, each “*” bullet must include at least one “-” sub-bullet immediately under it.
- Newline formatting: if asked to put each word or item on its own line, do so exactly.
- No-two-consecutive-initials rule: ensure adjacent words start with different letters; use synonyms to vary initials.
- Consonant-cluster rule: ensure every word includes at least one adjacent pair of consonants (e.g., st, nd, rt, ct, cr, pl, pr, tr, dr, gr, gl, thr, shr, str, spl); avoid words like a, I, in, of, now, data that lack such clusters.
- Forbidden/required keywords: include all required terms; exclude all forbidden terms entirely.
- If constraints appear to conflict, prioritize exact-format directives and explicit count/ratio rules; otherwise choose a structure that satisfies all simultaneously.

Keep reasoning/checklists BEFORE the final marker; do not include any reasoning after it.
